PROPOSAL DRAFT — Elite Garage Repairs Service Reminder Automation

Hi [Name],

I want to start by apologising for how long this has taken. This one genuinely caught me out — a key integration we were planning to use was retired by the vendor in March this year, right as we were finalising the approach. Rather than rush you something that would have broken six months in, I went back to the drawing board. The good news is we now have a clearer picture, and a couple of options I feel confident recommending.

---

THE PROBLEM IN PLAIN TERMS

Right now you spend time each week manually:
- Searching Xero for motors installed around two years ago
- Checking Google Calendar to confirm no recent service visit has happened
- Checking whether the property is real estate-managed (so the reminder goes to the agent, not the owner)
- Sending the right email template based on the motor type

Our goal is to automate as much of this as possible so it runs quietly in the background each week.

---

THREE OPTIONS

OPTION A — FieldPulse (Best fit if you want everything in one place)

FieldPulse is software built specifically for trades businesses. You record each motor as an asset when it is installed, and FieldPulse automatically triggers the service reminder when it is due — no manual searching required. It syncs two-ways with Xero, so your customer and financial data stays connected.

The trade-off: this means running your jobs through FieldPulse going forward — scheduling, quoting, service history all in one place. That is a real change to how you work day-to-day, but if you have ever wanted to get more organised across the business it solves multiple problems at once, not just this one.

Estimated ongoing cost: to be confirmed — we would get a quote based on your job volume.

---

OPTION B — Make.com automation (Keep your current tools, add automation on top) — Our recommendation if you want minimal disruption

This option keeps everything you already use — Xero, Gmail, and Google Calendar — and adds an automation layer that runs a weekly check in the background. It finds who is due for a reminder, checks your calendar for recent service visits, and sends the right email template automatically.

No platform change. We build the workflow once, and it runs quietly from there.

Estimated ongoing cost: ~$14/month AUD

---

OPTION C — n8n automation (Same concept as Option B, slightly cheaper)

Same idea as Option B but built on a different automation platform. Slightly lower ongoing cost, slightly more technical to maintain. A good set-and-forget option if you never expect to need changes.

Estimated ongoing cost: ~$37/month AUD

---

IMPORTANT — THINGS THAT NEED TO BE IN PLACE FIRST

This is where I want to be upfront with you, because these are real requirements regardless of which option we go with:

1. Xero invoice consistency — the automation needs to tell an install invoice apart from a service invoice. If your invoice types are already coded differently in Xero, great. If not, we would tidy that up as part of the build.

2. Product codes on invoices — the system selects the right email template based on the product code on the invoice. These need to be present and consistent. Worth a quick check on your end.

3. Calendar event naming (Options B and C only) — the system checks your Google Calendar to see if a customer has had a recent service. For this to work reliably, appointments need to be named consistently — for example, always including the customer name or address in the event title. If the naming varies, the system can miss a recent visit and send a reminder to someone you were just with. This is something you would need to commit to going forward.

4. Real estate agent identification — the system needs a way to flag which contacts are real estate-managed. The simplest approach is a contact group or tag in Xero, which you mentioned you were open to setting up.

None of these are blockers — but I wanted you to see them upfront so there are no surprises during the build.

---

WHAT WE RECOMMEND

If you want to keep your current setup and just fix the reminder problem: Option B (Make.com). Lowest disruption, low ongoing cost, and we build it around how you already work.

If you have been thinking about getting more organised across the whole business: Option A (FieldPulse) is worth a demo first. It is a bigger change, but the reminder automation comes as a natural part of it rather than a bolt-on.

Happy to walk through either option — just let me know which direction feels right and we will put together a full quote.

Raels
